newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Dow dip drives down Australian stocks at open.
newsitem.headline: Dow dip drives down Australian stocks at open.

text.p: Australian shares softened at the opening on Wednesday after the Dow dipped, breaking its record-breaking run.
Local leaders were mixed with little real direction apparent, most moving only a few cents either side of square.
At the opening, the All Ordinaries index lost 5.2 points to 2,376.8.
"The Dow slowed down but there is not really a lot to go on," said a Sydney broker. Expectations were for a single point finish in moderate trade.

Most interest in early trade came from mineral explorers, with interests in the Gawler Craton region in South Australia after Helix Resources released a drilling report confirming additional, significant gold mineralisation in its areas.
Helix shares rocketed 62 percent to an intraday high of A$3.00 (US$2.43), a more than six-fold increase in two weeks, before easing back to A$2.70.
Rises just shaded falls, while about 43 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
